A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PUP 3D-GS and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite appendix additions, renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and an EAGLES experiment.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a bonsai pruning result and background-error examples.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same Fisher-derived spatial sensitivity score, mean/scale parameters, patch computation and multi-round prune-refine procedure. Proposed extensions in the new appendix discussion are future work, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes, two Tanks & Temples scenes and two Deep Blending scenes, plus the EAGLES bicycle case. The additional bonsai test and background examples remain within this coverage; other pipelines are discussed without evaluation.

E2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds numerical comparisons using published Compact-3DGS bonsai scores and Compact-3DGS/Mini-Splatting compression ratios. These are literature-based comparisons, not reported reproductions. Comparator membership in Tables 1–11 is unchanged, and RadSplat is discussed without a scored evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 introduces a single-round bonsai test pruning 58.7% of Gaussians, matching the percentage attributed to Compact-3DGS. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged. The patch-size prose correction from 64×64 to 8×8 matches Table 6 in both versions and does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.9 and Figure 10 examine cases where PUP preserves foreground details but produces greater background L1 error than LightGaussian relative to the original 3D-GS renderings. Existing pruning-round, pruning-percentage, parameter and patch-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same interpolated means and standard deviations across pruning configurations. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical values in Tables 1–11 are unchanged. Appendix A.6 newly reports bonsai PSNR increasing from 32.25 to 32.55 at 58.7% pruning, alongside Compact-3DGS's cited 29.87 to 29.91; the different starting models preclude a matched-setting superiority conclusion. Figure 10 adds examples of greater background error.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), the Fisher/Hessian approximation and the Bayesian/Laplace derivation in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. The proposed extensions introduce no new formal definitions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about post-hoc sensitivity pruning, multi-round refinement, removing 90% of Gaussians and achieving a 3.56× average rendering speedup while preserving foreground detail.

C2.justification: Appendices A.7 and A.9 substantially expand applicability and limitation discussion beyond v2's convergence and memory limitations. They explain the foreground/background tradeoff, identify obstacles to directly pruning anchor-generated Gaussians, and discuss training-time pruning, depth/normal outputs and background-score reweighting as future directions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project website link, states that scoring the complete training-view set takes seconds in Section 5.2, and specifies the RTX A4000's 16GB memory in Section 7. These are additional access and resource disclosures, not documented changes to the implementation or hardware used.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Mini-Splatting, RadSplat, PGSR, Octree-GS and manifold-sampling uncertainty research. Sections 2.2 and A.6–A.7 extend positioning relative to concurrent pruning methods and potential applications while retaining the original research framing.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording improvements, revised author and acknowledgement text, and new appendix subsections with corresponding renumbering. Appendix A.2 corrects the patch-size typo to agree with Table 6. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, and Figure 3 revises contour styling and LPIPS colors without changing the displayed findings. A new background-error Figure 10 shares a page with Figure 9. The previous residual Figures 10–11 become Figures 11–12 with reordered scene rows and expanded captions; table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The background-error examples and explicit applicability boundaries make the consequences and scope of pruning clearer than in v2. Corrected patch-size prose, clearer graphics and added access/resource information also help. The gains are limited: the central evidence remains unchanged, and the new bonsai comparison uses different starting models rather than establishing superiority under matched conditions.
